title: Tiny Stories; the moon, the president and a question. What do we need more of?
text:
Tiny Stories; the moon, the president and a question. What do we need more of?
I saw the Earth from space and it made me think about humanity
Tiny Stories is a weekly writing prompt to get us not just writing, but also thinking. I’ll be moving them into a separate section so if you don’t want to receive them you’ll soon be able to opt out and just receive my regular posts. But I hope you’ll join in, because you’d be surprised how many writers find each other and find readers in the entries :)
What a surreal week. A week ago, I watched the Artemis II liftoff on NASA’s Live Stream, heading towards the moon. Last Friday they shared a photo of Christina Koch peering out of one of the cabin windows, looking back at Earth.
The photo gallery is magnificent. There’s one photo of Earth where you can see the Auroras above our little planet. Another shows a sliver of Earth, seen in eclipse.
Then yesterday morning, the President of America threatened to wipe out Iran’s entire civilization and I know it didn’t happen, but the contrast hit me. Hearing the wonder in the voices of the Artemis II crew, the way their voices crack with emotion as they look back at our little planet, and the reality of what’s happening on our planet.
Don’t we know there isn’t a backup planet?
It made me sit back and wonder — what do we need?
So here’s the prompt:
What do we need more of in this world? But don’t tell me straight up, okay? Write a scene to illustrate it and reveal the answer at the end. 150 words or less. You can check your wordcount at wordcounter.net
